Contributions of Microscopy
Study of cell biology limited until development of the compound light microscope
Continues to expand with development of electron microscopes and other molecular biology tools
Microscopy lead to clarifications of our definition of life, that all living things share basic characteristics:
Consist of organized parts
Obtain energy from surroundings
Perform chemical reactions
Change with time
Respond to environment
Reproduce
Separate their constant internal environment from the changing external environment
Share a common history 
common characteristics that show how cells are related to other living things
explanation: The study of cell biology was historically limited until the development of the compound light microscope, and the field continues to grow with advanced electron microscopes and molecular biology tools. Microscopy helped clarify the biological definition of life. All living organisms share several basic characteristics: they consist of organized parts, obtain energy from their surroundings, perform chemical reactions, change over time, respond to their environment, reproduce, separate their constant internal environment from the changing external environment, and share a common history showing their relatedness.

questions.q: What technological development initially broke the limitations on the study of cell biology?
questions.exp: The slide states that the study of cell biology was limited until the development of the compound light microscope.

questions.q: Which of the following is a basic characteristic of all living things identified through microscopy on this page?
opts: Having a cell wall for protection
Separating a constant internal environment from a changing external environment
Using sunlight directly as an energy source
questions.exp: One of the shared basic characteristics listed is that living things separate their constant internal environment from the changing external environment.
